# v2.96-dev

A follow-up to v2.95. Nothing in the application changes — this closes a gap in
the checks that guard what gets released.

## Changed

- **The privacy scan now stops a release instead of just mentioning it.** This
  product ships as a generic system, so the examples in its code, its
  documentation and these release notes must never contain real company names,
  real addresses or anything identifying a real person. v2.95 added a scan for
  that, but only as a warning — the idea being that an automated guess should
  never be able to halt a release on its own.

  That only works if somebody reads the warning. Releases now build and publish
  without anyone stepping in, so a warning had no reader: anything it spotted
  would have gone out to a public release page unseen. It now stops the release
  instead, and where it gets something wrong that can be overridden
  deliberately, which is a decision someone makes rather than a note nobody
  reads.

- **Two things it used to get wrong are fixed.** It no longer mistakes the
  credentials inside an update URL for somebody's email address, and it now
  recognises the example address already used in the user guide and the in-app
  help.

## A note on what it does and does not do

The scan recognises *patterns* — addresses at unfamiliar domains, file paths
naming a real account. It cannot recognise a real company, product or person's
name, and it deliberately does not try: the only way to check for those
automatically would be to keep a list of them in the project, which is exactly
what the rule exists to prevent. Those remain a human responsibility, and a
clean scan is not a clean bill of health.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do. No database changes, no configuration changes, and no change to
the application itself. If you run an installation, this release is functionally
identical to v2.95.
